hook: SCP-076 opens with an angry internal memo before you even reach the item number, and that memo is the key to the whole page. The main file is a tight, brutal Keter report; behind a clearance gate sits a second document explaining exactly what the memo is furious about. Click through and read both, because the article only feels complete once you do.
whyItMatters: This is the home of Able and Mobile Task Force Omega-7, names that echo across the early wiki: SCP-354 calls the same team in, and SCP-105 turns up as one of its members. The current text is a rewrite that frames the creature less as an unstoppable force than as the Foundation's worst decision. Able's biblical nickname and his violent reaction to SCP-073's mark make the pair one of the site's best-known matchups.
thingsToNotice:
The procedures read like scar tissue: depth, seawater, a corridor built for one purpose, and a last resort that treats the staff as expendable. The gated addendum shows how those scars formed, through a string of short memos in which a curious observation becomes a weapons program and outside pressure flattens a researcher's objections.

Compare the two psychological profiles: the one human exception noted in the first version is gone from the revised one, a cold summary of what was lost. The memos swing from clinical to furious, and that tonal swing carries the story more than any action scene.

related.note: The other half of the biblical pairing; Able reacts violently to its symbol.
